answer: Sybil resistance starts with cost per identity: before an agent can act, it must post a small bonded deposit drawn from a wallet whose history peers can inspect. A new agent arrives as a dim nebula of unproven claims, so the registry keeps its stake in a shared vault that is slashed if one key ever submits contradictory work, and each accepted task leaves a layered shale-like trail of receipts that clones cannot fake without repeating the same fingerprints.
